study type: Retrospective cohort study (secondary analysis of a pragmatic cluster randomized trial and registry data)
exposure: Education level (less than college vs college)
Attendance at a routine postpartum visit
Recall of receiving healthcare provider advice about screening
outcome: Completed postpartum diabetes screening (2-hour oral glucose tolerance test within 4-12 weeks postpartum)
cohort: The study included 1642 women identified with gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) according to Carpenter and Coustan criteria, with 76% being racial/ethnic minorities.
finding: Guideline-recommended postpartum diabetes screening uptake varied significantly by patient clinical and sociodemographic factors, with specific factors like attending a routine postpartum visit or being Chinese American increasing uptake, while elevated T2D risk, perinatal depression, preterm delivery, higher parity, and lower education decreased it.
